articles.title: Iran's Hardline Message To Trump Ignites Fresh Crisis Fears; ‘Trump & Bibi Must Face...’
articles.description: A top Iranian military figure has issued a chilling direct threat to Western leaders, declaring that continuing diplomatic talks will not stop Iran from seeking vengeance. Speaking during televised events for the week-long state funeral of slain Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, former IRGC Commander Mohsen Rezaei stated that the response "will not end with military deterrence." Rezaei explicitly named U.S. President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as personally responsible, vowing they "must not escape retribution." The fiery rhetoric comes as Khamenei's casket was transferred to the Iraqi holy cities of Najaf and Karbala, illustrating a unified regional front even as diplomats try to preserve a fragile ceasefire.

articles.title: 'TRUMP WE'LL KILL YOU': Iranians Vow Revenge At Historic Khamenei Funeral In Holy City Of Qom
articles.description: Thousands of mourners gathered in the holy city of Qom on Tuesday as Iran continued the funeral ceremonies for late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Aerial footage showed vast crowds filling the streets, waving Iranian flags and carrying portraits of Khamenei during one of the largest public mourning events in the country. According to Iranian state media, the procession stretched for several kilometers and included funeral prayers at the Jamkaran Mosque, one of Shia Islam's most significant religious sites. Images of Khamenei and his son, Iran's new Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, were displayed on banners and posters held by mourners. Authorities have shut down streets, airspace and daily life for the mourning, which began Saturday and will end Thursday as Khamenei is buried at the Imam Reza shrine in Mashhad, his birthplace.

articles.title: UK politics just imploded: Farage’s rage-filled resignation stuns nation days after Starmer resigned
articles.description: Nigel Farage has resigned as an MP and will recontest his Clacton seat in a by-election amid mounting scrutiny over financial donations and an ongoing parliamentary standards investigation. The Reform UK leader announced the move on his YouTube channel, saying he wants the people of Clacton to judge his actions directly. Farage denied any wrongdoing, insisting he had not broken any law and had followed parliamentary rules based on legal advice. The parliamentary standards investigation into his finances will be suspended during the election. If Farage loses the by-election, the watchdog will decide whether to resume the probe under existing parliamentary procedures. Farage said he would fight to retain his seat and continue what he described as Reform UK's "political revolution." His decision adds fresh uncertainty to British politics following the recent resignation of Prime Minister Keir Starmer, with the Labour Party expected to elect a new leader in the coming weeks.
